title: Generation of Dynamical Environmental Conditions using a High-Throughput Microfluidic Device
protocol: Design the microfluidic multiplexer with 18 inlets, each controlled by an individual valve and peristaltic pump.
Widen the peristaltic pump control channels to 200 µm and connect them to 10 flow lines.
Design a shear-free culture chamber consisting of a lower cell culture chamber (400 µm x 400 µm x 150 µm) and a higher buffer layer (400 µm x 400 µm x 75 µm).
Duplicate the culture unit to form a 30 x 50 matrix layout covering an area of approximately 7 cm by 5 cm.
Fabricate replica molding using UV lithography on silicon wafer according to standard photolithography protocol.
Spin coat 5 mL of SU-8 3025 negative photoresist on the silicon wafer at 500 rpm for 10 seconds and then 3000 rpm for 30 seconds.
Place the wafer on a hotplate at 65 °C for 2 minutes, followed by 95 °C for 10 minutes.
Cool the wafer down to room temperature.
Align the wafer and mask in the holder of the aligner and cure the exposed photoresist for 18 seconds.
Ramp up the wafer to 95°C at 110°C/h from room temperature and keep it for at least 40 min.
Dip the wafer in the developing solution (SU-8 developer) and agitate it for 2.5 min.
Cover the wafer with a glass Petri dish and bake at 65°C for 2 min, then ramp up to 160°C at 120°C/h and keep it for 3 hours.
Spin coat 7 mL of SU-8 3075 negative photoresist on the wafer using parameters from step 2.1.1.1.
Soft bake the wafer and align the mask with markers on the wafer.
Exposure to light source for 24 seconds to cure the exposed photoresist.
Dip the wafer in the developing solution (SU-8 developer) and agitate it for 4 minutes and 40 seconds.
Hard bake the wafer to strengthen the complex structure.
Repeat steps 2.1.2.1 through 2.1.2.3 to fabricate a 75 µm-high chamber structure that stacks on the layer structure.
Spin coat 5 mL of AZ 50x positive photoresist on the above wafer using parameters from step 2.1.1.1.
Soft bake the wafer and align the mask well with markers on the wafer.
Keep the light source on for 20 s and off immediately for 30 s.
Repeat the light on/off procedure in 5 circles.
Dip the wafer into matched developer and agitate it for about 8 min to wash off redundant photoresist.
Hard bake the patterned wafer to strengthen the model.
Treat the patterned and blank silicon wafers with dimethylchlorosilane for 15 min.
Prepare 3 portions of PDMS gel in a ratio of 10:1 (monomer/catalyst) corresponding to 50 g of flow layer, 20 g of control layer 2, and 20 g of membrane, respectively.
Cast 50 g of PDMS gel on the patterned silicon wafer.
De-gas the cast PDMS for 1-2 hours in a vacuum chamber at -0.85 MPa to copy the flow layer.
Degas the 2 portions of 20 g of PDMS and spin them on the patterned wafer and a blank silicon wafer at 2000-2800 rpm for 30 s as to prepare control and membrane layers.
Put the PDMS-covered wafers into a ventilating oven for 60 min at 80 °C for incubation.
Align and bond different layers together using a customized optical device (zoom in 100x) and plasma etching machine.
Keep the bonded chip in a ventilating oven for 2 hours at 80 °C to enhance bonding.
Punch inlet holes on the chip.
Bond the chip onto a PDMS-coated coverslip and cure it for at least 12 hours at 80 °C before use.
Connect miniature pneumatic solenoid valves to the control layer of the chip.
Open the customized MATLAB graphical user interface to link and control the switch.
Set the closing pressures of push-up PDMS membrane valves to 25 psi.
Deliver dynamically changing combinatorial/sequential inputs to designated chambers by timely on-off of the valves.
Maintain standard culture conditions (37 °C, 5% CO2) on the microscope for at least 5 hours.
Fill the chip with coating medium and incubate it at standard culture conditions for at least one hour.
Flush the chip with phosphate-buffered saline (PBS) or cell culture medium (Dulbecco's Modified Eagle's medium, DMEM).
Harvest cells at 80% confluency.
Resuspend harvested cells using culture media (DMEM) at a density of ~10^6/mL.
Load cells into the chip by pressurizing the cell-containing solution.
Visualize the matrix of culture chambers using a 10x objective lens in bright field to affirm and define the location coordinates of each chamber of the 30 by 50 chamber matrix.
Transform the objective lens to the 20x or 40x, then select the location coordinates of the desired chamber and the translational stage moves to the assigned position after confirmation.
Fine tune the x, y, z focal plane to get an optimal image.
Optimize light intensity, exposure time, and other imaging parameters individually for each channel (i.e., bright-field and fluorescence imaging).
Set the interval and duration of the imaging cycle, save the path, and then start imaging.
